chapterTag.category: AP Calc BC BC-1 — Advanced Integration

body.en: Unit 6BC covers the advanced analytical integration techniques required on the AP Calculus BC exam: reversing the Product Rule through Integration by Parts, decomposing rational expressions via Partial Fractions, and evaluating Improper Integrals involving infinite boundaries or integrand singularities using rigorous limit definitions.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Integration by Parts & The LIATE Priority Protocol

body.en: Integration by Parts transforms an intractable integral of a product of functions into a simpler integral by redistributing derivatives.

label.en: ● Theorem & Formal Analytical Proof · Integration by Parts Formula

body.en:
Theorem: Let \(u(x)\) and \(v(x)\) be continuously differentiable functions on an interval. Then: \[ \int u(x) v'(x)\,dx = u(x)v(x) - \int v(x)u'(x)\,dx, \] or equivalently in differential notation: \[ \int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du. \]

Proof: By the Product Rule for differentiation: \[ \frac{d}{dx}[u(x)v(x)] = u'(x)v(x) + u(x)v'(x). \] Integrating both sides with respect to \(x\): \[ \int \frac{d}{dx}[u(x)v(x)]\,dx = \int u'(x)v(x)\,dx + \int u(x)v'(x)\,dx. \] By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, the left-hand side is \(u(x)v(x)\): \[ u(x)v(x) = \int v(x)u'(x)\,dx + \int u(x)v'(x)\,dx. \] Subtracting \(\int v(x)u'(x)\,dx\) from both sides: \[ \int u(x)v'(x)\,dx = u(x)v(x) - \int v(x)u'(x)\,dx. \quad \blacksquare \]

The LIATE Strategy: To choose \(u\), select the function that appears earliest in the list: Logarithmic (\(\ln x\)), Inverse trigonometric (\(\arctan x\)), Algebraic (\(x^n\)), Trigonometric (\(\sin x\)), Exponential (\(e^x\)). The remaining factor becomes \(dv\).

label.en: Level 1 (Foundations) — Worked Example · Single and Definite Integration by Parts

body.en:
Problem: Evaluate the definite integral \(\int_1^e x^3 \ln(x)\,dx\).

Step 1 · Choose \(u\) and \(dv\) via LIATE:
Logarithmic precedes Algebraic, so let: \[ u = \ln(x) \implies du = \frac{1}{x}\,dx. \] \[ dv = x^3\,dx \implies v = \frac{x^4}{4}. \]

Step 2 · Apply Definite Parts Formula: \[ \int_1^e x^3 \ln(x)\,dx = \left[ \frac{x^4}{4}\ln(x) \right]_1^e - \int_1^e \left(\frac{x^4}{4}\right)\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)dx. \]

Step 3 · Simplify and Integrate: \[ = \left( \frac{e^4}{4}\ln(e) - \frac{1^4}{4}\ln(1) \right) - \frac{1}{4}\int_1^e x^3\,dx = \frac{e^4}{4} - \frac{1}{4}\left[ \frac{x^4}{4} \right]_1^e. \] \[ = \frac{e^4}{4} - \frac{1}{16}(e^4 - 1) = \frac{4e^4 - e^4 + 1}{16} = \mathbf{\frac{3e^4 + 1}{16}}. \]

label.en: Worked Example D — Instantaneous Rate of Change & Tangent Line

body.en:
Let \( f(x) = 5x^3 - x^2 + 4 \). Find the instantaneous rate of change \( f'(5) \).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Differentiate term-by-term using the power rule: \( f'(x) = 15x^2 - 2x \).
  2. Substitute \( x = 5 \): \( f'(5) = 15(5)^2 - 2(5) = 375 - 10 = \mathbf{365} \).

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

Evaluate the indefinite integral \(\int \arctan(x)\,dx\).

solution.en: Use LIATE: \(u = \arctan(x) \implies du = \frac{1}{1+x^2}\,dx\), and \(dv = dx \implies v = x\). Applying parts: \[ \int \arctan(x)\,dx = x\arctan(x) - \int \frac{x}{1+x^2}\,dx. \] For the second integral, let \(w = 1+x^2 \implies dw = 2x\,dx\): \[ \int \frac{x}{1+x^2}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\ln(1+x^2). \] Thus: \[ \mathbf{x\arctan(x) - \frac{1}{2}\ln(1+x^2) + C}. \]

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Tabular Integration & Partial Fraction Decomposition

body.en: Accelerate repeated integration by parts with the Tabular Method, and integrate rational functions \(\frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}\) where \(\deg(P) < \deg(Q)\) by decomposing the integrand into partial fractions.

If \(\deg(P) \ge \deg(Q)\), polynomial long division must be performed first. Once proper:

  • Distinct Linear Factors: If \(Q(x) = (x - r_1)(x - r_2)\), decompose into: \[ \frac{A}{x - r_1} + \frac{B}{x - r_2}. \] Solve using the Heaviside Cover-Up Method: Multiply by \((x - r_1)\) and evaluate at \(x = r_1\).
  • Repeated Linear Factors: If \(Q(x) = (x - r)^2\), decompose into: \[ \frac{A}{x - r} + \frac{B}{(x - r)^2}. \]
  • Irreducible Quadratic Factors: If \(Q(x) = x^2 + a^2\), the numerator must be linear \(Ax + B\), leading to logarithms and \(\arctan\) antiderivatives.

label.en: Level 2 (Medium) — Worked Example · Partial Fractions with Heaviside Method

body.en:
Problem: Evaluate the indefinite integral \(\int \frac{7x - 5}{x^2 - x - 6}\,dx\).

Step 1 · Factor the Denominator: \[ x^2 - x - 6 = (x - 3)(x + 2). \]

Step 2 · Decompose into Partial Fractions: \[ \frac{7x - 5}{(x - 3)(x + 2)} = \frac{A}{x - 3} + \frac{B}{x + 2} \implies 7x - 5 = A(x + 2) + B(x - 3). \]

Step 3 · Heaviside Cover-Up Evaluation:
• For \(x = 3\): \(7(3) - 5 = A(3 + 2) \implies 16 = 5A \implies A = \frac{16}{5}\).
• For \(x = -2\): \(7(-2) - 5 = B(-2 - 3) \implies -19 = -5B \implies B = \frac{19}{5}\).

Step 4 · Integrate: \[ \int \left( \frac{16/5}{x - 3} + \frac{19/5}{x + 2} \right) dx = \mathbf{\frac{16}{5}\ln|x - 3| + \frac{19}{5}\ln|x + 2| + C}. \]

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

Evaluate \(\int x^3 \sin(2x)\,dx\) using the Tabular Method.

solution.en:
Tabulate signs, derivatives of \(x^3\), and antiderivatives of \(\sin(2x)\):
• \((+) \quad x^3 \qquad\qquad -\frac{1}{2}\cos(2x)\)
• \((-) \quad 3x^2 \qquad\quad -\frac{1}{4}\sin(2x)\)
• \((+) \quad 6x \qquad\qquad \frac{1}{8}\cos(2x)\)
• \((-) \quad 6 \qquad\qquad\quad \frac{1}{16}\sin(2x)\)
• \((+) \quad 0 \qquad\qquad -\frac{1}{32}\cos(2x)\)

Sum the diagonal products: \[ = -\frac{1}{2}x^3\cos(2x) + \frac{3}{4}x^2\sin(2x) + \frac{3}{4}x\cos(2x) - \frac{3}{8}\sin(2x) + C. \] Group terms: \[ = \mathbf{\left(-\frac{1}{2}x^3 + \frac{3}{4}x\right)\cos(2x) + \left(\frac{3}{4}x^2 - \frac{3}{8}\right)\sin(2x) + C}. \]

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced / AP FRQ — Improper Integrals & The p-Convergence Theorem

body.en: Improper integrals occur when an integration interval is unbounded (Type I: \([a, \infty)\), \((-\infty, b]\), or \((-\infty, \infty)\)) or when the integrand possesses an infinite discontinuity (Type II: vertical asymptote at an endpoint or interior point).

label.en: ● Theorem & Formal Analytical Proof · Convergence of the p-Integral

body.en:
Theorem: The improper integral \(\displaystyle\int_1^\infty \frac{1}{x^p}\,dx\) converges if and only if \(p > 1\). For \(p > 1\), its value is \(\frac{1}{p - 1}\). It diverges for all \(p \le 1\).

Proof: Rewrite as a limit: \[ \int_1^\infty \frac{1}{x^p}\,dx = \lim_{b \to \infty} \int_1^b x^{-p}\,dx. \]

Case 1 (\(p = 1\)): \[ \lim_{b \to \infty} \int_1^b \frac{1}{x}\,dx = \lim_{b \to \infty} [\ln x]_1^b = \lim_{b \to \infty} (\ln b - 0) = \infty. \quad (\text{Diverges}) \]

Case 2 (\(p \neq 1\)): \[ \int_1^b x^{-p}\,dx = \left[ \frac{x^{1-p}}{1-p} \right]_1^b = \frac{b^{1-p} - 1}{1-p} = \frac{1}{1-p}\left(\frac{1}{b^{p-1}} - 1\right). \]

• If \(p > 1\), then \(p - 1 > 0\), so \(\lim_{b\to\infty} \frac{1}{b^{p-1}} = 0\): \[ \lim_{b \to \infty} \frac{1}{1-p}\left(\frac{1}{b^{p-1}} - 1\right) = \frac{0 - 1}{1 - p} = \frac{1}{p - 1}. \quad (\text{Converges}) \]

• If \(p < 1\), then \(1 - p > 0\), so \(\lim_{b\to\infty} b^{1-p} = \infty\). \quad (\text{Diverges})

Hence \(\int_1^\infty x^{-p}\,dx\) converges \(\iff p > 1\). \(\blacksquare\)

label.en: Level 3 (Advanced/FRQ) — Worked Example · Interior Infinite Discontinuity (Type II)

body.en:
Problem: Evaluate the improper integral \(\int_{-1}^2 \frac{1}{x^4}\,dx\) or show that it diverges.

Fatal AP Trap: Blindly integrating using the power rule yields \(\left[ -\frac{1}{3x^3} \right]_{-1}^2 = -\frac{1}{24} - \left(\frac{1}{3}\right) = -\frac{9}{24} = -\frac{3}{8}\). This is catastrophic: \(f(x) = \frac{1}{x^4} > 0\) everywhere, so its area cannot be negative! The integrand has an infinite vertical asymptote at \(x = 0\) inside the interval \([-1, 2]\).

Step 1 · Split at the Singularity: \[ \int_{-1}^2 \frac{1}{x^4}\,dx = \int_{-1}^0 \frac{1}{x^4}\,dx + \int_0^2 \frac{1}{x^4}\,dx. \]

Step 2 · Express Each as a One-Sided Limit: \[ \int_{-1}^0 \frac{1}{x^4}\,dx = \lim_{c \to 0^-} \int_{-1}^c x^{-4}\,dx = \lim_{c \to 0^-} \left[ -\frac{1}{3x^3} \right]_{-1}^c = \lim_{c \to 0^-} \left( -\frac{1}{3c^3} - \frac{1}{3} \right). \] As \(c \to 0^-\), \(c^3 \to 0^-\), so \(-\frac{1}{3c^3} \to +\infty\).

Conclusion: Since the left sub-integral diverges to \(\infty\), the entire improper integral diverges.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced / AP FRQ

Evaluate the improper integral \(\int_0^\infty x e^{-2x}\,dx\) or establish that it diverges.

solution.en: Rewrite with limit notation: \[ \lim_{b \to \infty} \int_0^b x e^{-2x}\,dx. \] Use integration by parts: \(u = x \implies du = dx\), \(dv = e^{-2x}\,dx \implies v = -\frac{1}{2}e^{-2x}\). \[ \int x e^{-2x}\,dx = -\frac{1}{2}x e^{-2x} - \int \left(-\frac{1}{2}e^{-2x}\right)dx = -\frac{1}{2}x e^{-2x} - \frac{1}{4}e^{-2x}. \] Evaluate from 0 to \(b\): \[ \lim_{b \to \infty} \left[ -\frac{1}{2}b e^{-2b} - \frac{1}{4}e^{-2b} - \left(0 - \frac{1}{4}e^0\right) \right]. \] By L'Hôpital's Rule, \(\lim_{b\to\infty} \frac{b}{e^{2b}} = \lim_{b\to\infty} \frac{1}{2e^{2b}} = 0\), and \(\lim_{b\to\infty} e^{-2b} = 0\). Therefore: \[ 0 - 0 - \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right) = \mathbf{\frac{1}{4}}. \] The improper integral converges to \(\frac{1}{4}\).

question.en: [Unit 6BC · Advanced Integration Techniques · Practice 4] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 6t + 6 \), evaluate \( g(10) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 72 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 10 \): \( g(10) = 6(10) + 6 = \mathbf{66} \). Setting \( 6t + 6 = 72 \) gives \( 6t = 66 \implies t = \mathbf{11} \).
